title: Answer on the diagram, not only about it
statement: When the skill is reading a diagram, make its elements selectable and include steps answered on the diagram itself, such as tracing a path, not only sentences picked about it.
detail: An audit of a Grade 5 lesson on reading a food-web diagram ruled that a rendering whose elements can't be addressed fails the construct, and it blocked a planned guided step in which the student sequences the arrows on the diagram itself rather than tapping a passage sentence. The fix gave every node and arrow an id and made them selectable, and the guided step now has the child tap two arrows in order on the map, with the dashed connector and the third arrow live as wrong targets. The lesson's scored release item still asks about an arrow through sentence options, which the audit upheld.
against: Sentence options about a diagram still have a place: the audit upheld a release item that asks about an arrow through sentence options (grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/GRADE5-AUDIT.md, lines 295-296), so the rule asks for some steps on the diagram, not every step.
